text: Withdrawals are capped at 5000 per account per day, a limit the plan never mentions.
The 'daily' withdrawal total is never reset, so it is really a lifetime cap of 5000 per account.
The withdrawal limit applies only to withdrawals, so transfers can move any amount out of an account.
When a withdrawal would both overdraw and exceed the limit, it is reported as insufficient funds because that check runs first.
Amounts are rounded to cents with half-up rounding (Math.round), which runs on floating-point values.
Rounding happens after the positivity check, so an amount like 0.001 is accepted, rounds to 0, and records a zero-value entry.
Balances are stored as floating-point numbers instead of integer cents, so totals can drift.
The positivity check rejects NaN but accepts Infinity and amounts with any number of decimal places.
Overdrafts are not allowed, but a withdrawal or transfer may take the balance down to exactly zero.
A repeated transaction id returns success and does nothing, without checking that the account, amount or operation type match the original.
A retry gets a plain ok, the same reply as a new operation, so the caller cannot tell it was a duplicate.
Transaction ids share one global namespace across all accounts and operation types, and they are kept forever.
Rejected operations do not mark their transaction id as used, so the same id can later succeed with different data.
The amount is validated before the duplicate check, so a retry of an accepted id with a bad amount is rejected instead of acknowledged.
Deposits, withdrawals and transfers silently create any account that does not exist, and there is no check for valid account ids.
A rejected withdrawal or transfer still creates the accounts it named.
Unknown accounts report a balance of 0 and an empty history rather than an error.
Transaction ids are not validated, so empty or blank ids are accepted.
A transfer writes the same transaction id into both accounts' histories, with no counterparty, timestamp or resulting balance on either entry.
Rejection reasons are the fixed strings 'invalid-amount', 'insufficient-funds' and 'daily-limit'.
A transfer to the same account is accepted, leaves the balance unchanged and records two history entries.
